newsitem.title: HONG KONG: GOLF-LANGER FALTERS IN MASTERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LANGER FALTERS IN MASTERS.

text.p: Bernhard Langer's hopes of his
first tournament win in 13 months faded on Saturday when he had
a triple bogey in the third round of the Alfred Dunhill Masters
and fell three strokes behind leader Scott Laycock of Australia.
Germany's Langer, whose last win was at the European Open,
seemed to be coasting after an eagle at the 12th but his tee
shot at the par-three 15th landed behind a tree and he had to
hit out sideways. He made the green in three and three-putted
for a six.
Langer ended with a two-under 69 for a three-round total of
202, 11 below par, while Laycock hit a faultless 65 to take the
outright lead in the $500,000 event.
"I was a bit unlucky (at the 15th) as the ball took a bad
bounce and went behind the tree," said Langer, who won on this
course at the 1991 Hong Kong Open. "There is nothing I can do
about it -- I am only three behind and I can still win."
Laycock, chasing his first title after two years as a
professional, had six birdies to upstage playing partner Langer.
"I do not think I have any weaknesses but I will find out
tomorrow -- I have never led a tournament before," said the
25-year-old Australian.
Thailand's Boonchu Ruangkit, who had a bogey at the last for
a 67, and Hsieh Yu-shu of Taiwan, with a third-round 68, were
tied for second, two shots behind Laycock.
Spain's Seve Ballesteros, fighting a bad cough with the help
of some Chinese medicine, had a typically rollercoaster
five-under-par 66 to move up the leaderboard at six-under-par
"I did not sleep too well and had to call the doctor. He
gave me some Chinese medicine which tasted horrible," said
Ballesteros, who had six birdies but dropped shots after several
typically wayward tee shots.
"Sometimes when you are not feeling well you play better. My
golf is getting better every day -- maybe if we were playing 10
rounds I would have a chance to win."
World number three Ernie Els of South Africa also had a
five-under-par 66 and was seven shots off the pace while
Scotland's Colin Montgomerie, the European number one, shot his
third successive 69 but was unhappy with his game.
"I am not playing very well," Montgomerie complained after a
bogey at the last. "I have not played well for the last month
and when it's like this you know that mistakes are going to
happen. The ball is not going where I am aiming."
